title: Variables and Primitive Types
learning_objectives: You can assign numbers, strings, and booleans to variables
You can inspect runtime types using type()

prerequisites_check.question: What is the key principle behind Variables and Primitive Types?
prerequisites_check.explanation: Python requires adhering to clear lexical and semantic rules.

explanation_simple: Variables are labeled storage boxes in computer memory. You write the box name, an equals sign, and the value you want to keep inside.
explanation_technical: Python variables are reference names pointing to PyObject heap allocations. Primitive values like int, float, bool, and str are immutable.

worked_examples.title: Declaring variables of different types
worked_examples.code:
age = 25
gpa = 3.9
is_student = True
print(age, gpa, is_student)

predict_the_output.code:
age = 25
gpa = 3.9
is_student = True
print(age, gpa, is_student)

summary: Variables point to immutable primitive values and dynamically track their type at runtime.
